title: Third-Party Assessment Engagement Playbook and Evidence Formatting
content:
Purpose and audience:
This playbook is intended for the security & compliance team, solutions engineering, and any third-party assessment vendors engaging with Redwood Inference. It documents an engagement cadence, minimal evidence artifacts we provide, a lightweight audit-log schema that vendors and our SIEM ingestion expect, and pragmatic automation recipes to produce evidence bundles with sensitive-data controls.

High-level goals:
- Minimize back-and-forth with assessors by standardizing evidence formats.
- Maintain least-privileged access while supporting timely evidence delivery.
- Provide reproducible export steps so logs, RBAC snapshots, and config artifacts can be delivered consistently.
- Ensure exports contain enough context for triage and remediation planning.

Engagement cadence (recommended):
1) Kickoff (Day 0): 30–60 min call covering scope, allowed tools, data zones, and SLAs for evidence requests. Share this playbook and a sample evidence bundle.
2) Scoping (Day 0–3): Security team and assessor align on target systems, timeframe for logs, and non-production workflows.
3) Evidence window (Day 3–N): We prepare and deliver evidence bundles incrementally.
4) Findings review (T+3 days from evidence delivery): Joint review meeting for each findings tranche.
5) Remediation tracking and verification (Ongoing): Use JIRA board SEC-****.

Scope matrix (example):
- Included: control plane audit logs, RBAC role map snapshot (RBAC v2), service-to-service auth logs, bastion session metadata, SIEM-exported alerts for the selected window.
- Excluded unless explicitly requested: full message payloads from customer-owned instances, PII-containing request bodies, production S3 object contents.

RBAC v2 snapshot requirements (minimum):
- Format: CSV or newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) with one row per assignment.
- Fields we provide: timestamp, snapshot_id, principal_id, principal_type (user/service), assigned_roles (comma-separated), assignment_source (ui, api, terraform), scope (org, project, model-id), granted_by, grant_request_id.
- Verification points for assessors: cross-check role permissions against the permission matrix (separate spreadsheet), confirm no overly-broad wildcard grants exist for production projects.

Audit log schema (canonical fields we export):
We aim to provide a compact, consistent schema regardless of backend. Field names below are the canonical mapping we use when creating evidence bundles for assessors.
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_id (uuid)
- request_id (opaque id tied to upstream request path)
- actor_id (user/service id)
- actor_type (user, service, iam-role)
- actor_roles_before (semicolon-separated)
- actor_roles_after (semicolon-separated)
- action (verb, e.g., model.invoke, role.assign, key.create)
- resource_type (model, route, secret, compute-pool)
- resource_id (logical id)
- result (success|failure|denied)
- outcome_code (numeric or string error code)
- ip_address
- user_agent
- trace_id (distributed trace)
- host_region
- ingest_source (api|console|batch-job)
- raw_metadata_ref (pointer to archived raw event if needed)

Note: For privacy we redact request/response payloads unless explicitly authorized. raw_metadata_ref points to a hashed artifact stored in a restricted evidence bucket.

SIEM export recipe (one-line cookbook):
- Target window: 72h pre/post target event or as scoped by assessor.
- Aggregation: NDJSON with canonical fields above.
- Indexing hints: Elastic index pattern: redwood-audit-%{+YYYY.MM.dd} ; Splunk sourcetype: redwood:audit; Timestamp in ISO will be parsed as @timestamp by both systems.
- Common mappings to include in the bundle: event_id, request_id, actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, result, host_region, trace_id.

Packaging evidence bundles (automated flow):
1) Input: start/end timestamps and scope filters (service, org, project).
2) Run audit-export script (infra/audit-scripts/export-audit.sh) to pull normalized NDJSON for the window into the evidence staging folder.
3) Run rbac-snapshot script to emit RBAC CSV and a permissions matrix extract.
4) Run anonymize-layer that masks PII fields and replaces direct customer identifiers with consistent pseudonyms.
5) Produce a manifest.txt listing files, checksums (sha256), and the filter criteria used to generate logs.
6) Upload to restricted evidence bucket with object lifecycle: 30 days then archive.

Example manifest.txt format (plaintext lines):
- evidence-bundle-id: EVID-2024-11-04-03
- start: 2024-11-01T00:00:00Z
- end: 2024-11-04T00:00:00Z
- files: audit.ndjson.gz, rbac-snapshot.csv, permission-matrix.csv, infra-config-snaps.tar.gz
- sha256(audit.ndjson.gz): <hex>
- redaction: request_payloads=REDACTED, customer_ids=PSEUDO_###

Evidence automation safeguards (must-haves):
- All generation runs must be performed by an identity with least privilege via ephemeral role; the run is recorded in an evidence_generation audit event.
- Default redaction template applied; PII removal is reviewed by privacy SME before handoff.
- Access to the evidence bucket is time-bound and IP-restricted for vendor consumption.

Sample findings summary template (for assessor findings once received):
- Finding ID: SEC-F-XXXX
- Short title: e.g., Missing denial for internal API route
- Severity: Critical/High/Medium/Low
- Affected scope: e.g., production/model-service-us-east-1
- Evidence refs: bundle id, audit event ids, rbac snapshot row ids
- Root cause hypothesis: short paragraph
- Immediate remediation (48h): actions and owners
- Long-term fix (30–90d): PRs, config changes, validation tests
- Verification steps: steps to confirm remediation and artifacts required

Remediation plan skeleton (internal use):
- Owner (primary)
- Secondary owner (security reviewer)
- Task list with JIRA tickets and acceptance criteria
- Timeline with checkpoints and verification meeting date

Operational play notes (less formal):
- If an assessor asks for full raw request bodies for a single request, route to security-sme@redwood for approval; default is deny without explicit signed NDA appendix.
- For RBAC mismatches found during review, create a temporary canary role to reproduce the permission vector and collect a short DVR of the action paths.
- Keep staged evidence bundles small—prefer multiple targeted bundles rather than one massive tarball. It speeds triage and reduces blast radius.

Appendix: quick commands (examples)
- Export NDJSON (example): ./export-audit.sh --start 2024-11-01T00:00:00Z --end 2024-11-04T00:00:00Z --scope project:prod-models --out audit.ndjson
- Snapshot RBAC: python infra/scripts/rbac_snapshot.py --format csv --out rbac-snapshot.csv
- Create bundle: ./mk_evidence_bundle.sh --audit audit.ndjson --rbac rbac-snapshot.csv --manifest manifest.txt --encrypt vendor-key.pub

Open questions (for the next review):
- Agree on a minimal set of role names that must be included in every RBAC snapshot for easier cross-team comparisons.
- Can the privacy team sign a standing approval for redaction rules for Class A findings to avoid case-by-case delays?

Notes to self (working):
- Follow up: add a small sample NDJSON with three synthetic events that demonstrate role.assign, model.invoke, and key.rotate.
- Reach out to infra team to add event: assignment_source into newest audit stream (tracked in JIRA: SEC-7992).

End of playbook.
